A. Award Bid SP2717 and Construction Contract to Sully Miller Contracting Company for the FY 25-26 Annual Paving Project and Accept Transportation Development Act Grant
Recommended Action
Staff recommends that the City Council:
1. Adopt a finding of Categorical Exemption pursuant to Section 15301 of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines;
2. Award Bid #SP2717 to Sully Miller Contracting Company for the FY 20 25-26 Annual Paving Project for the Public Works Department;
3. Authorize the City Manager to negotiate and execute a contract with Sully Miller Contracting Company in an amount not to exceed $7,591,163 (including a 15% contingency) ;
4. Authorize the City Manager to accept a grant awarded in the amount of $ 211,000 from the L os Angeles Metro Transportation Development Act (TDA) Funds for FY 2025 - 26 Annual Paving Project in the Department of Transportation , and to accept all grant renewals;
5. Authorize the City Manager to execute all necessary documents to accept the grant an d all grant renewals ; and
6. Authorize budget amendment as outlined in the Financial Impacts & Budget Actions section of this repo r t (requires 5 votes).

C. Request of Councilmember Zwick, Councilmember Raskin, and Mayor Pro Tem Torosis that the City Council direct the City Manager to return with options for revising development standards to effectively implement Housing Element Program 1.C. Despite prior best efforts, our City continues to see underutilized parking lots remain vacant on commercial corridors. Updates to development standards may be needed in order to incentivize housing projects along transit corridors and near a future “Great Park.” Specifically, additional incentives may include new zoning/ development standards for housing projects on surface parking lots associated with commercial corridors that match the zoning/ development standards of the commercial corridors they abut and removal of the requirement that new housing projects replace code-required parking at 50% New Item Received. 8/6/2026

Butterfly Brawl’s mission is to combine high-level boxing, entertainment, and philanthropy in support of cancer-related causes. This year, fundraising efforts will focus on the Santa Monica Police Activities League (PAL) and the American Cancer Society that supports those affected by cancer New Item Received. 8/6/2026
